spans.text: Bentchaphobia: "I don't want bread—I don't want to have to bentch!" Why do we go to great lengths to avoid having to bentch? The simple answer is that bentching is long and we're in a rush. But I'd like to take it a bit deeper and offer two thoughts on this subject for you to consider. And they apply not only to the full Birkas Ha'mazon, but to Al Ha'michyah and Borei Nefashos as well.

1. In our world of plenty ("When I was your age..."), it's so easy to take stuff for granted. We go to the store and find tons of all kinds of food right there for us—in all seasons. What does it take for all that food to get to the store? A lot of miracles! The sun has to rise, it must rain at the right time and the right amount, seeds must grow—you get the idea. And there are so many miracles involved in us having the ability to eat the food, taste it, digest it, etc. These miracles are no less amazing than the manna in the desert. It's just that we're used to these miracles since they happen all the time (except when there are hurricanes, floods, sickness—again, you get the idea). That's why we don't feel the need to spend all that time bentching—it's a burden for "no real good reason." This is similar to Pesukei D'Zimrah, which many people find annoying—"Why do I have to praise Hashem so much? Does He (chas v'shalom) struggle with His self-esteem?" Here too, we so quickly take our world and our miraculous history for granted. Hashem does not need our bentching, and He does not need our Pesukei D'Zimrah. We need to say it in order to better appreciate—and thus enjoy—all that we have!

2. We don't like to owe other people favors. We don't like to be beholden to others. "I'm fine, I can do it all myself!" But we can't do anything without Hashem's help! And that idea can make some people feel uncomortable because they like to be in control. By bentching (and again—the same for Pesukei D'Zimrah) we are helping ourselves focus on the concept that though we must do as much as we can, in the end, nothing happens without Hashem's help.
On weekdays, some start with the following:

The focus of this chapter is that even after the destruction of the Beis Hamikdash, when Yerushalayim was physically destroyed by Bavel, its spirit still lives on in all our hearts! As we enjoy our meal and our material abundance, we remember that we are not fully "home"; we must not forget that Yerushalayim is not yet what it should be!

always felt we were foreigners living in a foreign land. It was never "home." אִם אֶשְׁכָּחֵךְ—If I should ever forget Yerushalayim (and view our exile as my permanent home and the final destination of Bnei Yisrael)—may I lose my strength, skills, and abilities (for what good are they if I have lost sight of our true goal?).

שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת—When Hashem takes us out of our galus and returns us to Yerushalayim, it will be as if waking up from a dream (our confusion will begin to clear). We will sing praises to Hashem, and the nations of the world will proclaim: "Hashem has done great miracles for His chosen nation" (that's us!). Please, Hashem, take us out of our galus! הַזֹּרְעִים בְּדִמְעָה—May those who "planted with tears" (kept Torah and mitzvos even when it was difficult and not popular) harvest (collect their reward) with happiness!

תְּהִלַּת יְהֹוָה יְדַבֶּר פִּי—May my mouth declare the praises of Hashem (so powerfully and sincerely) וִיבָרֵךְ כָּל בָּשָׂר—that everyone שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד—(even today while we are still in galus, will be so impacted by my words and actions that they too) will bless Hashem and see Him as the Source for all blessings—for eternity! וַאֲנַחְנוּ נְבָרֵךְ יָהּ—Each of us (in our way, based on our own life experiences) will

thank Hashem and see Him as the Source of blessing in our individual lives; מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם—now and forever (no matter what will happen)! (To sum it all up in one word:) הַלְלוּיָהּ—whatever happens, praise Hashem!
הוֹדוּ—Give thanks to Hashem, for all that He does is good; His kindness is eternal, though in truth it is beyond our ability to truly thank Hashem properly for all He does!

(The Leader calls us to action and says to us:) We must make the world realize (by how we speak and how we conduct ourselves daily) that Hashem is the Source of everything (and certainly of the meal we just ate!).
(And we respond:) May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that Hashem is the Source of everything!
(The Leader responds:) May everyone (including me!), everywhere, and forever, see that Hashem is the Source of everything!

(The Leader continues:) With the permission (of all seated here), let us now thank Hashem (our God) and proclaim that He is the Source of everything that we have just eaten (notwithstanding how much effort we put in preparing this meal!).

(And we respond:) We thank Hashem (our God) and proclaim that He is the Source of everything that we have just eaten (notwithstanding how much effort we put in preparing this meal!), and it is only through His goodness that we are able to live!
(And everyone concludes by proclaiming:) Hashem is truly the Source of everything, and all that He does is for our good!

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; You take care of us and You rule the entire world; and You provide all the needs for the entire world with kindness and compassion (even when we are not so deserving!). You provide food to all living things, thanks to Your great chessed. And because of Your constant goodness, we have never lacked food, and we will never lack anything, for You feed all, sustain all, do good for all the creatures You have created. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַזָּן אֶת הַכֹּל—Who provides food for all.

נוֹדֶה לְךָ—We thank You, Hashem, for: giving us a wonderful and spacious land; taking us out of Egypt and freeing us from slavery; giving us the mitzvah of bris milah; for Your Torah that You taught us; for Your mitzvos that You gave us; for life, goodness, and kindness that You granted us; and for continually taking care of us, constantly!

(וְ) עַל הַנִּסִּים וְעַל הַפֻּרְקָן—(We also thank You) for our miraculous rescue; for the mighty acts and victories; and for the battles (from which You allowed us to emerge victorious) that You performed for our ancestors in those days at this season.

In—בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָהוּ On Chanukah: the days of the Kohen Gadol Matisyahu the Chashmonai and his children, the despotic Syrian-Greek empire rose up against Your people (Bnei Yisrael), to try to make them forget Your Torah and abandon the Torah way of life. But You, in Your great mercy, stood by the Torah-true Jews in their time of distress and championed their cause, defended their rights, and avenged the wrongs done to them. You made the weak and few (army of the Chashmonaim) victorious

over the stronger and more numerous (Greek army). You made the Jews who had remained pure from the immorality of the Greek culture (טְהוֹרִים), who had remained righteous and loyal to Torah standards (צַדִּיקִים), and who remained diligent in the study of Torah (עוֹסְקֵי תּוֹרָתֶךָ) victorious over the Jews who had taken the side of the Greeks, adopted the immorality of Greek culture (טְמֵאִים) and רְשָׁעִים), and deliberately tried to eradicate Torah study (זֵדִים). All the world recognized Your power and greatness, and You brought about a great liberating victory for Your nation. Then Your children cleaned up and purified the Beis Hamikdash and lit the Menorah and instituted these eight days of Chanukah for giving thanks and praise to You.

In—בִּימֵי מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר On Purim: the days of Mordechai and Esther, in the capital city of Shushan, the evil Haman rose up to exterminate all Jews, young and old, on the thirteenth day of Adar. But You in Your great mercy thwarted his plan and caused his scheme against us to boomerang onto his own head, and he and his sons were hung on the gallows.

For everything we thank You, Hashem, and acknowledge that You are the Source of everything! May all who live constantly recognize that You are the Source of everything and thank You forever, as it says in the Torah: (When) you will eat and will be satisfied, then you shall recognize that He is the Source of everything and thank Him for the good land He has given you. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; עַל הָאָרֶץ וְעַל הַמָּזוֹן—(and specifically) of our land and our food.

רַחֵם (נָא)—(Please) Hashem, have mercy on Your nation Bnei Yisrael (and take us out of galus), and on Your city of Yerushalayim and on Zion (that it should be rebuilt) and on the royal house of David HaMelech (that Mashiach should come) and on the Beis Hamikdash (that it should be rebuilt). Hashem, our Father Who takes care of us, please feed and sustain us, and send us relief from all our difficulties. And we should never need the help of others, but rather only Your direct help, which is always available and generous. This way we will never feel ashamed or humiliated.

רְצֵה וְהַחֲלִיצֵנוּ—May it please You, Hashem, to strengthen us through Your mitzvos, and through the mitzvah of Shabbos. For this day is great, separate and unique, when we refrain from work and we rest, out of love (for the Shabbos), just as You commanded us. May it be Your

will to grant us tranquility, so that there shall be no distress, sadness, or sorrow on the day of our rest. And let us see the consolation of Zion, Your city, and the rebuilding of Yerushalayim, for You control all deliverance and consolation.

Hashem,—אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout our history, please view us favorably, and take into account our special relationship with You, and the promises You made to our ancestors: the promise to bring Mashiach and to rebuild Yerushalayim and restore its holiness, and to remember all of Bnei Yisrael everywhere, to deliver us from our exiles (physical and spiritual), and to grant our requests and have mercy on us (even if we are not deserving), and to give us all life and peace on this day of: Rosh Chodesh/Pesach/Sukkos. Give us all goodness, blessings, and life (even if we are not all deserving), show compassion on us, because we have turned to You for help because we know that You, Hashem, control everything, and You are a compassionate and merciful King.
וּבְנֵה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִיר הַקֹּדֶשׁ בִּמְהֵרָה—And rebuild Yerushalayim, the holy city, speedily and in our lifetime! בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; בּוֹנֵה בְרַחֲמָיו

יְרוּשָׁלַיִם—Who, with mercy (even though we are not deserving), builds Yerushalayim (present tense—since every step of our galus is a necessary part of the process of the eventual permanent rebuilding of Yerushalayim). אָמֵן—And that is absolutely true and I hope it will happen soon!

You, בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהוָה—You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; אֱלֹהֵינוּ—You take care of us; מֶלֶךְ—and You rule the entire world; You are our Father, our King, our mighty One, our Creator, our Redeemer, and You have shaped us (into Your nation). You are קדוש—separate and far removed from this physical world; we too are also "קְדוֹשִׁים"—we are separate and removed from the values and the "norms" of the material world (look at the miracle of our survival!). You are our Shepherd (Who has guided us through our miraculous history). You are the Good King Who does good to everyone; שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם הוּא הֵטִיב הוּא מֵטִיב הוּא יֵיטִיב לָנוּ—for each and every day (whether we realize it or not) Hashem Himself has done good for us (in the past); Hashem Himself does good for us (now); and (and we believe that in the future) Hashem Himself will (continue to) do good for us—granting us chessed and kindness (helping us even when we do not deserve all this good), prosperity, success, relief from our troubles, salvation, support, a livelihood, and a life of peace and all good things! וּמִכָּל טוֹב לְעוֹלָם—אַל יְחַסְּרֵנוּ—May He never cause us to lack any good things!
הָרַחֲמָן—May Hashem, Who is compassionate

May Hashem, Who is compassionate, bless (my father, my teacher) the master of this house; and (my mother, my teacher) the mistress of this house; them, their household, their children, and all that is theirs; (If you are at your own table:) me (and my wife/husband and my children and grandchildren) and all that is ours; (and all who ate at this table); Just as He blessed our Avos, Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov, so may He bless all of us together with a perfect brachah and let us all say: אָמֵן—that is absolutely true, and I hope it will happen soon!

Up in Heaven, may merits be found for all those mentioned above and for all of us at this table (and all Bnei Yisrael) to ensure everlasting peace (in their homes and our homes). May we receive brachah and kindness from Hashem and may we find grace and good understanding in the eyes of Hashem and in the eyes of people.

spans.text: FAQ: What? It certainly doesn't look like Hashem "provides all of us with all we need"! There are people out there really suffering!
ANSWER: That is the classic question of tzaddik v'ra lo—why the righteous suffer! See Appendix 2.

בשבת מוסיפים: רְצֵה וְהַחֲלִיצֵנוּ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ, וּבְמִצְוַת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי הַשַּׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה, כִּי יוֹם זֶה גָּדוֹל וְקָדוֹשׁ הוּא לְפָנֶיךָ, לִשְׁבַּת בּוֹ וְלָנוּחַ בּוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה כְּמִצְוַת רְצוֹנֶךָ, וּבִרְצוֹנְךָ הָנִיחַ לָנוּ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ, שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא צָרָה וְיָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה בְּיוֹם מְנוּחָתֵנוּ, וְהַרְאֵנוּ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּנֶחָמַת צִיּוֹן עִירֶךָ, וּבְבִנְיַן יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִיר קָדְשֶׁךָ, כִּי אַתָּה הוּא בַּעַל הַיְשׁוּעוֹת וּבַעַל הַנֶּחָמוֹת׃

FAQ:
It certainly doesn't look like Hashem "does good to everyone"! There are people out there really suffering! And my life is a mess! I certainly don't see "prosperity, success, relief from our troubles..."!

ANSWER:
Correct! Once again, that is the classic (and very important) question of tzaddik v'ra lo, why the righteous suffer! See Appendix 2.
On Shabbos: May Hashem, Who is compassionate, let us inherit that time (when Mashiach comes), which will be entirely Shabbos and a rest for life everlasting.

On Rosh Chodesh: הָרַחֲמָן—May Hashem, Who is compassionate, renew this coming month for us for good and for blessing. בראש חדש: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יְחַדֵּשׁ עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לְטוֹבָה וְלִבְרָכָה׃
On Yom Tov: הָרַחֲמָן—May Hashem, Who is compassionate, let us inherit that day (when Mashiach comes), which is all good. ביום טוב: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יַנְחִילֵנוּ יוֹם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ טוֹב׃
On Sukkos: הָרַחֲמָן—May Hashem, Who is compassionate, restore for us the fallen sukkah of David HaMelech. בסוכות: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יָקִים לָנוּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד הַנּוֹפֶלֶת׃
